Date: 2026-07-14T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: prompt harvest + safety/redaction checklist

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Recap: demoed (1) summarization + structured extraction from intake forms, (2) triage routing predictor, and (3) policy redaction layer. You confirmed 10k monthly active cases and an initial pilot scope of 5k transactions/month.
- Immediate ask from Redwood: a) a representative set of customer prompts (happy path + edge cases), b) a short list of PII/sensitive fields you want redacted at generation time, and c) any high-risk examples where hallucination or privacy would be unacceptable.

For model guidance, our recommended starting points for this workload are:
- Redwood-Base-7B (low-cost, good for fast iterations)
- Redwood-Large-34B-q4 (balanced latency/capacity for seam-of-production accuracy)
- Redwood-Instruction-13B (if you need stronger instruction-following on structured outputs)

Benchmarks and docs I referenced during the call:
- Redwood inference benchmarks: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/inference (look at the extraction/seq2seq rows)
- Prompt template & collection spreadsheet (editable): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEf

Please send the prompt CSV and any "must redact" rules by EOD Wed so we can draft a focused eval and produce a short canary run (500 transactions) next week.

Attachments: none from our side yet.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20 min sync if that helps.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0192

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@clearwave.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt harvest + safety/redaction checklist

Ben — thanks, nice recap. Attaching two files that should help:
- clearwave_prompts_v1.csv (sample prompts from triage forms + clinician notes)
- high_risk_examples.txt (three transcripts where recall/hallucination caused problems)

A few notes on redaction:
- Primary sensitive fields: patient_name, MRN, date_of_birth, provider_license_number. We want those redacted from both inputs that go into model prompts and any generated outputs returned to non-clinical users.
- For PII in free-text clinician notes, we currently prefer a rule-based preprocessor + model-level mask for anything that looks like an MRN (pattern match).

Also important: we will need an audit trail for any redaction decisions (who/when/why) — does Redwood produce that automatically in your private deployments?

Question on models: low-latency is important (90th percentile < 400ms for the short queries). If we go with Redwood-Large-34B-q4, can you share observed 90th pctl numbers for 128-token generation?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product, ClearWave Health
agomez@clearwave.com

Attachments:
- clearwave_prompts_v1.csv (8KB)
- high_risk_examples.txt (3KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Alicia — got the files, thanks — they look really useful. Quick responses below and a proposed eval plan:

Redaction / audit trail:
- Yes, our Private deployment includes redaction hooks + structured audit log entries (who/when/transform). We can include the audit export in CSV/JSON for your compliance team.

Latency numbers (90th pctl, 128 tokens, single-request):
- Redwood-Base-7B: ~120ms
- Redwood-Instruction-13B: ~210ms
- Redwood-Large-34B-q4: ~360ms
(These are observed in our EU-west1 dedicated tier; we can run region-specific runs for your org.)

Proposed canary eval (500 transactions):
- Dataset: 300 happy-path prompts from your CSV + 200 edge-case / high-risk items (from your high_risk_examples.txt).
- Metrics: extraction F1, hallucination rate (manual labels on a 50-sample subset), latency (p50/p90), and redaction false negatives.
- Deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet + recommended model + suggested quantization/kv-cache settings.

Can you confirm the PII redaction list (patient_name, MRN, DOB, provider_license_number) and whether we should also redact partial dates (month/year) in outputs? That affects our conservative vs permissive masking strategy.

I’ll also upload a short eval harness and a prompt-capture template to the Drive link and share a HubSpot deal with the canary plan.

Next step: if you confirm the redaction fields, I’ll schedule the canary for next Tue (07/21) and loop in our Solutions Engineer for the run.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Ben — quick plan from my side:

1) Canary infra
- We can run the 500-transaction canary in Private with audit-exports enabled. Will need the signed NDA (requesting from procurement). If you can get the NDA back this week, we can schedule the run for 07/21 as proposed.

2) Redaction strategy
- Start with two-step approach: 1) lightweight regex-based preprocessor for MRN patterns and obvious tokens (fast, deterministic); 2) model-based NER/masking as a second-pass for ambiguous free-text items. We will log both transforms in the audit CSV so ClearWave can reconcile.

3) Model selection and eval
- Agree to validate Redwood-Large-34B-q4 p90 in us-west1. Karthik will run a small micro-benchmark (50 synthetic prompts + 128-token gen) and report p50/p90 numbers by EOD 7/18. If p90 exceeds 420ms, we’ll recommend Instruction-13B quantized for the canary.

4) Compliance artifacts
- We have a SOC2 export sample + data-retention policy doc. I’ll attach the NDA template in a follow-up.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm NDA status and upload signed copy to the Drive folder.
- Karthik: run the micro-benchmark and post results to the Drive.
- Ben: confirm whether partial dates (month/year) should be redacted — Alicia, awaiting your confirmation.

I’ll draft the canary runbook and share by EOD 7/18.
